title: Boss: review the albums design doc
summary: A real design doc lands in your review queue. Build the reviewer's tools: find numbers without units, split the doc into sections, and produce the review comments a senior would leave. Then design the capstone on the board.

steps.title: The doc in your review queue
body: A colleague asks for your review before Thursday's design review. Every team copies the same template, so
half of a good review can be automated. This is the doc:
Users share photos one by one. Album requests are the top support topic.
- Create an album and add up to 500 photos.
- 4,000,000 DAU, 2 album views each per day.
- Each album row is 2 KB; 40 new albums per second at peak.
- Albums table in the existing PostgreSQL cluster, keyed by album_id.
- Album pages cached at the CDN for 60 s.
- Behind a feature flag: 1%, then 10%, then 100% over two weeks.
Read it as a reviewer first. The peak looks plausible (4 M x 2 / 86,400 is about 93 average, so 280 is 3x).
But there is no security or observability section, "2" and "40" have no clear unit, there is one
alternative, and nothing says how to roll back. Your tools should find exactly that.

steps.title: Numbers without units
prompt: Write `List<string> UnitlessNumbers(string text)`. Split `text` on whitespace. For each token, trim the
characters `, . ; : ( )` from both ends. The token is a **number** if it starts with a digit and contains only
digits, `,` and `.` (so `4,000,000` and `1.5` are numbers; `300ms`, `99.9%` and `2026-12-01` are not).
A number **has a unit** when the next token, trimmed the same way and lower-cased, is one of:
`ms s seconds min minutes h hours days weeks months years % qps rps kb mb gb tb gbps mbps dau users requests reads writes bytes instances cores x`
Return the trimmed numbers that have no unit, in order. A number at the very end has no unit.
hints: `text.Split((char[]?)null, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)` splits on any whitespace; `Trim(params char[])` trims the punctuation.
A number: `char.IsDigit(t[0]) && t.All(c => char.IsDigit(c) || c == ',' || c == '.')`. Then look at `tokens[i + 1]`.
template: Dojo.Eq("servers is not a unit", new List<string> { "12" }, UnitlessNumbers("Peak 280 QPS and 12 servers."));
Dojo.Eq("every number has a unit", new List<string>(), UnitlessNumbers("Latency 300 ms, payload 2 KB."));
Dojo.Eq("commas inside numbers, punctuation after units", new List<string> { "2" }, UnitlessNumbers("4,000,000 DAU, 2 album views each per day."));
Dojo.Eq("a number at the end", new List<string> { "500" }, UnitlessNumbers("Monthly cost 500"));
Dojo.Eq("attached units and decimals with x", new List<string>(), UnitlessNumbers("p99 under 300ms at 1.5 x the peak"));
Dojo.Eq("brackets are trimmed", new List<string> { "3" }, UnitlessNumbers("We need 3 (three) caches"));
Dojo.Eq("dates and percentages are not numbers", new List<string>(), UnitlessNumbers("Launch 2026-12-01 at 99.9% availability"));

steps.title: Split the doc into sections
prompt: Write `Dictionary<string, List<string>> Sections(string[] doc)`. A line that starts with `## ` (after trimming)
opens a section titled by the rest of the line, trimmed. Every following **non-empty** line, trimmed, belongs to
it until the next `## `. Lines before the first section (the `# ` title) are ignored. Look-ups must ignore
case: build the dictionary with `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`.
Your `UnitlessNumbers` is in the starter; you will use both in the last step.
solution: else if (current is not null && line.Length > 0) current.Add(line);
hints: Keep a `List<string>? current`: a `## ` line creates a new list and stores it under its title.
Other lines go into `current` when it is not null and the trimmed line is not empty.

Dojo.Eq("the title line is not a section", false, dojoS.ContainsKey("Design: shared albums for Snapshare"));
Dojo.Eq("lines keep their order", "- Peak 280 QPS for album pages.", dojoS["Estimates"][1]);
var dojoMessy = Sections(new[] { "intro", "  ## Goals  ", "", "   - fast   ", "## Empty", "## Goals two", "x" });
Dojo.Eq("blank lines are skipped and lines trimmed", new List<string> { "- fast" }, dojoMessy["goals"]);
Dojo.Eq("an empty section still exists", 0, dojoMessy["Empty"].Count);

steps.title: The review comments
prompt: Write `List<string> Review(string[] doc)` using `Sections` and `UnitlessNumbers` (both in the starter).
Return comments in this order:
1. `"missing: <title>"` for each missing required section, in this order: `Context`, `Goals`, `Non-goals`,
`Estimates`, `Proposal`, `Alternatives considered`, `Security and privacy`, `Observability`, `Rollout`.
2. `"no rollback plan"` if there is a `Rollout` section and none of its lines contains `rollback` or
`roll back` (any case).
3. `"unitless number in Estimates: <n>"` for each unitless number in the `Estimates` section (its lines
joined with a space), in order.
4. `"fewer than two alternatives"` if there is an `Alternatives considered` section with fewer than two lines
starting with `- `.
For the albums doc you should get six comments; for the fixed version, none.

steps.title: Capstone: design photo sharing on the board
prompt: Now be the author, not the reviewer. In the **System design board**, the capstone gives you only the users
and their traffic: uploads of large photos and many more views. Design the service: object storage with
presigned uploads so photos never pass through your app servers, a CDN for views, a cache, app servers and a
database spread across zones. Meet the latency, availability (with a zone failure) and budget goals the board
shows, then write down, as you would in the doc, the one trade-off you would raise in review.
steps.explain: Everything in this topic shows up in one design: estimates decide the sizes, the edge and object storage carry the bytes, the cache carries the reads, and headroom across zones carries the failure. The dashboard is your load-test report.
